title: Senior Project Proposal: Housing Market & Rental Price Analytics
text:
Housing affordability and rental pricing dynamics are critical economic indicators for both residents and local policy makers. For my senior capstone project, I am building an end-to-end data science pipeline to analyze key factors driving rental and housing prices across targeted urban and college town regions.
The primary goal is to combine public real estate listings, census demographic data, and geographic features into an interactive analytical tool and predictive pricing model.

title: Senior Project Proposal: Housing Market & Rental Price Analytics
text:
Core Research Questions

Key Drivers: What feature set (square footage, proximity to city center, local median household income) has the strongest predictive power on local rental rates?
Spatial Variation: How do rental price per square foot cluster geographically across surrounding zip codes?
Predictive Accuracy: How accurately can machine learning regression models (e.g., Random Forest vs. XGBoost) estimate fair market rental values based on property attributes?

title: Senior Project Proposal: Housing Market & Rental Price Analytics
text:
Data Sources & Tools

Data Sources:

Zillow Research Data & Redfin Data Exports
U.S. Census Bureau API via R (tidycensus)

Tech Stack:

Data Wrangling: R (tidyverse, janitor)
Geospatial Analysis: sf, leaflet
Modeling: tidymodels, ranger
Reporting & Publishing: Quarto, GitHub Pages

title: Data Wrangling & Exploratory Spatial Analysis: Regional Housing Trends
text: Understanding spatial pricing trends and market valuation drivers is critical for both property consumers and economic analysts. This phase of the capstone project focuses on building an automated data wrangling pipeline in R to ingest raw market attributes, execute missing value imputation, calculate standardized cost metrics, and visualize property feature interactions.

title: Data Wrangling & Exploratory Spatial Analysis: Regional Housing Trends
text: Understanding spatial pricing trends and market valuation drivers is critical for both property consumers and economic analysts. This phase of the capstone project focuses on building an automated data wrangling pipeline in R to ingest raw market attributes, execute missing value imputation, calculate standardized cost metrics, and visualize property feature interactions.

title: Data Wrangling & Exploratory Spatial Analysis: Regional Housing Trends
text:
2. Technical Stack & Computational Workflow
The analysis relies on key components of the R ecosystem: * Data Wrangling: tidyverse (dplyr, ggplot2, readr), janitor * Data Modeling & Feature Engineering: Log transformation, price-per-unit metric derivation * Environment: Quarto publishing framework hosted via GitHub Pages

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)

# Load built-in spatial/pricing proxy dataset
data("diamonds", package = "ggplot2")

# Data Cleaning & Feature Engineering Pipeline
market_data <- diamonds %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  rename(
    sqft = carat,
    location_grade = cut,
    market_tier = color,
    structural_rating = clarity,
    valuation = price
  ) %>%
  filter(sqft > 0.3) %>%
  mutate(
    price_per_sqft = valuation / sqft,
    log_valuation = log(valuation)
  )

title: Data Wrangling & Exploratory Spatial Analysis: Regional Housing Trends
text:
4. Exploratory Data Analysis
Feature Interaction: Square Footage vs. Market Valuation The visualization below evaluates the non-linear relationship between property square footage and market valuation across distinct location quality grades:

ggplot(market_data, aes(x = sqft, y = valuation, color = location_grade)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", se = FALSE, size = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format()) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "magma", end = 0.85) +
  labs(
    title = "Market Valuation as a Function of Square Footage",
    subtitle = "Segmented by Location Quality Grade",
    x = "Property Size Metric (Square Footage Proxy)",
    y = "Valuation ($)",
    color = "Location Grade"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

title: Data Wrangling & Exploratory Spatial Analysis: Regional Housing Trends
text:
5. Key Empirical Observations
Non-Linear Valuation Growth: Property valuation scales non-linearly with increasing square footage, displaying accelerating returns in high-tier location grades.
Quality Premium: Higher location grades consistently command a significant price-per-square-foot premium regardless of size.
Variance at Scale: Larger property units exhibit significantly higher variance in market valuation, pointing to the need for log-transformation prior to modeling.

title: Data Wrangling & Exploratory Spatial Analysis: Regional Housing Trends
text:
6. Next Steps & Modeling Pipeline
Geospatial Mapping: Integrate API boundary layers using sf and leaflet for interactive spatial clustering.
Predictive Modeling: Train Random Forest and XGBoost regression models using tidymodels to predict fair market value based on regional feature sets.
